interface.title: Crop Stress Prediction from Satellite Data (Streamlit app)
interface.field: Agricultural remote sensing / crop monitoring with machine learning
interface.stage_of_work: Looking at and explaining the results of models already trained to forecast vegetation stress (no training or data upload in the app)
interface.what_it_is_for: Explore Random Forest and XGBoost forecasts of vegetation stress 2–4 weeks ahead (from Sentinel-2 indices plus weather) for 36 field sites in Afghanistan, the Netherlands and New Zealand: on a map, as each site's history, as a comparison between countries, as satellite data coverage, and as a SHAP waterfall for one site and period.

data.note: Committed predictions, models and metrics load at startup with no user action. Periods run from Jan 2019 to Dec 2024 in 16-day composites, with 2023–2024 as the test set. The map's basemap tiles (CARTO/OSM) never loaded in this offline sandbox, so the markers sit on a grey background. Positions and popups still work.

tree.general: Find where vegetation stress is forecast, judge how trustworthy the forecast is, and understand why a given forecast was made
tree.specific: Use the RF/XGBoost crop-stress models to find stressed field sites at each site's most recent 16-day period, check model accuracy and satellite coverage, and explain single predictions with SHAP

It also redraws the map colours, the history probabilities and the SHAP waterfall. The Country comparison and Data coverage tabs do not change with it

features.name: Per-site time-series chart with paired data table
features.general: Pick one item from a list, filtered by region, and see its measured signal and model-predicted risk over time as an interactive chart, with a sortable table of predicted vs. actual outcome per period
features.specific: Location history: the Location dropdown is filtered by the sidebar Country. A Vega-Lite line chart shows NDVI (prior period) and predicted stress probability for 2019–2024, with hover tooltips, wheel zoom, double-click reset and a toolbar (Show data, Download as PNG, Copy Vega-Lite spec, Fullscreen). Below it is a dataframe of period_start, NDVI_lag1, ndvi_zscore, stress, pred_stress and pred_stress_prob, newest first
steps: Choose a Location
Scan the two lines for dips and spikes
Hover or zoom the chart to read exact values
Scroll to the table to compare predicted vs. actual stress per period
Download the chart as PNG
serves_tasks: Plot one site's index history alongside its predicted risk
Inspect and export the time-series chart
Check forecasts against what actually happened, period by period

features.name: Single-prediction SHAP waterfall explainer
features.general: Choose one item and one time point, then see an additive breakdown of how each input moved the model's output from the baseline to the final value, with the threshold decision and the true outcome spelled out
features.specific: How a prediction is made: Location and Period dropdowns draw a SHAP waterfall (top 11 features plus 'N other features'). The x-axis is probability units for Random Forest and log-odds for XGBoost with a sigmoid conversion. A caption states final probability vs. tuned threshold → predicted label, and the actual label. Period keeps its previous value when Location changes. A Fullscreen button is available
steps: Choose a Location (all 36 sites, independent of the Country filter)
Choose a Period (that site's dates, newest first); it does not reset when Location changes, so check it committed
Read the pink and blue bars from E[f(X)] to f(x)
Read the caption's probability vs. threshold and the actual outcome
Optionally switch the model and compare
serves_tasks: Show how each input pushed one prediction up or down, and the final call against the threshold
Compare the explanation of the same prediction under a second model

features.name: Observation coverage and gap diagnostics
features.general: Summarise how complete a set of repeated observations is: overall coverage, valid counts per site against the maximum, and the distribution of gaps between consecutive valid observations
features.specific: Data coverage tab: metric cards (4,448 / 4,932 usable composites, 90.2%, 16-day cadence), a matplotlib bar chart of valid cloud-free composites per location out of 137 coloured by country, and a histogram of days between consecutive usable readings with hover counts

Scan the per-site bars against the 137 line
Hover the gap histogram bars to count longer gaps
serves_tasks: Look at gaps between consecutive observations

features.name: Cross-group comparison panel
features.general: Compare groups side by side on how often the condition occurs, how well the reference model does in each group, and their seasonal baseline
features.specific: Country comparison: a bar chart of stress incidence by country, a per-country test-set table (n, stress_rate, accuracy, f1_stress) and a line chart of mean NDVI by month for each country. The table always comes from metrics.json for the best model (XGBoost) and ignores the Model and Country selectors
steps: Read incidence bars

Compare monthly NDVI curves to see seasonal offsets
